_comment: The Codex document schema vocabulary — the single list of node and mark
types the editor understands. ADR-0012 turns this list into a safety
boundary: ProseMirror silently drops content that does not match its
schema, so anything NOT named here must be captured and preserved rather
than parsed. The Go layer reads this file to decide what to capture; the
editor reads its TypeScript mirror to decide what to register.
The two must not drift, and the direction of drift is not symmetric:
a type the editor registers but Go omits is merely captured when it did
not need to be (annoying, safe), while a type Go omits from capture
because it believes the editor handles it, when the editor does not, is
silent data loss. web/src/lib/codex/schema.test.ts reads this file and
fails on any difference in either direction.
_positionComment: Capture has to choose between the block placeholder and the inline one,
and it cannot ask an unknown type which it is — so it decides from the
position instead. These two lists are what make that decision agree with
the editor's real content models. Getting one wrong is not silent, though:
if a placeholder lands where ProseMirror will not accept it, the node is
dropped, Restore reports the id as missing, and publish refuses the write
_projectedAttrsComment: The attributes the markdown projection reads by name.
These are the second half of the vocabulary, and they fail differently
from the type names above. A type the editor omits is silent data loss;
an ATTRIBUTE renamed on one side loses nothing at write time — the page
publishes, the document stores correctly, and the content quietly stops
being findable, because internal/core/wiki/doc/text.go looked for a name
that is no longer there. Nothing fails until somebody searches for a
panel's kind or an expand's summary line and does not find it.
So the list lives here rather than in either language: schema.test.ts
checks the TypeScript mirror against it, extensions.test.ts checks that
the real ProseMirror schema declares every attribute named, and
text_projection_test.go checks that the projection actually reads each
one — a table whose key set must equal this manifest, so an attribute
added here without a projection to go with it fails rather than ships.
